fields.meta_title: Catering Order Form Builder for Event Caterers | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a catering order form that tracks guest count changes, lists special meals by name, and staffs each event from the order. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Catering Order Form That Keeps the Final Count Straight
fields.hero_description: Build a catering order form that logs the event date, guest count, and special meals to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: The Questions a Caterer Asks on Every Call
fields.features_subheading: Each answer on the form replaces a follow-up call. The kitchen and the event captain work from the same order the client sent.
fields.feature_1:
Event basics before the menu

The form asks for the event date, the venue address, and the phone number of whoever is on site that day. A driver who cannot find the loading door calls that person directly.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that follow the service

The client picks drop-off, buffet, or plated service, and the next questions follow that pick. Plated service asks for each guest's entree, and drop-off asks who receives the food.
fields.feature_3:
One guest count, every change kept

Clients revise the guest count on their original order until the final count date you set. Each change saves as a numbered revision, and the newest count sits at the top.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts for new orders and late changes

The app emails you or posts in Slack when an order arrives or a client edits the count. A reminder goes to the client a week before the final count date, while edits are open.
fields.feature_5:
Orders saved in a database you own

Every order saves as a row in a database you own, with no response caps in June or December. Filter the rows by event date and next week's events line up with their counts.
fields.feature_6:
A signed order that reaches your books

The client can sign the order on the form before you hold the date. The app can then send the order total to QuickBooks or Xero through its API, where you raise the invoice.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Caterers and the Orders They Take
fields.tab_content_1:
The final count drops to 132 by May 27

Saltmarsh Table Catering plans Ilse Varga's June 13 wedding reception from a single order. She booked 140 guests, with the final count due May 30. On May 27 she lowered it to 132 on that same order, which now reads revision 2, and the kitchen plans for 132.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each special lunch with its guest's name

Quillfern Kitchen packs an 85-person lunch for the Ostend Valley Growers Association's spring meeting. Organizer Teodor Mbeki listed 9 vegetarian and 3 gluten-free lunches, each under the attendee who asked for it. The packing list shows 73 standard boxes and 12 lids labeled by name.
fields.tab_content_3:
On site by 4:30 pm with 4 servers and a captain

Brackenridge Events staffs every buffet at 1 server per 30 guests, plus a captain. Wren Okonjo booked a 120-guest buffet with service at 6:00 pm. Her order came back with 4 servers and 1 captain, and the staff sheet puts them on site at 4:30 pm, 90 minutes before service.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any order inside 72 hours waits for Odalys

Larkspur Lane Catering confirms orders placed at least 72 hours ahead without anyone touching them. Jonah Pell ordered breakfast for 30 on Tuesday at 9:00 am, for Thursday at 8:00 am, 47 hours out. Owner Odalys Ferro got an email asking her to approve it, and Jonah's confirmation waited for her yes.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Catering Order Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to turn your phone questions and event rules into a catering order form that books each event.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the questions you ask every new client on the phone: the date, the venue, the guest count, the service style, and dietary needs. Each one becomes a field, so the order arrives complete.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick a final count date and a minimum notice period, and write each as a number, such as 14 days before the event and 72 hours for new orders. The form needs both to lock counts and hold late orders.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide how a guest count becomes a crew, such as 1 server per 30 guests at a buffet. Add the arrival time you want, counted back from service, so the staff sheet is complete when the order lands.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a dietary question that asks for the guest's name next to each special meal. A vegetarian plate or an allergy note then reaches the right seat or the right box, not only the right event.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your questions and rules into one prompt, and Emergent builds the form, its logic, and the database behind it. When your menu or rules move, ask for the change in plain English the same way.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Open the form as a client
fields.howto_step_6_des: Place a test order for an event you catered last month, typing it in as the client would. Then change its guest count and check that the revision saves and the alert reaches you before you share it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send the link with every quote
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share the link in your quote email and on the catering page of your website. Every order placed from it lands in the same database, next to the events you have already booked.

faq_plan.q: What is a catering order form?
faq_plan.a: A catering order form is the record a client fills in to book food for an event, and the caterer plans the kitchen and the staff from it. It can be a catering order form PDF that the client prints and returns, or a web form that saves each order as it is sent.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a catering order form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the questions you ask clients, your final count date, and the notice you need. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, and you change either one by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a catering order form template include?
faq_plan.a: A catering order form template should cover the event and the people: when and where it happens, who to call on site, and how many guests are coming. Then add the menu choices, a dietary question, and the final count date written as a calendar date.

faq_plan.q: What other forms should I build alongside a catering order form?
faq_plan.a: Start with the order, then add the forms that come up every week, such as a tasting request, a staff availability sheet, or a uniform order form for servers' shirts and aprons. Catering order forms cover the client side. Emergent builds each of the others from its own plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: How much notice should a catering order form require?
faq_plan.a: Require as much notice as your kitchen needs to buy and prep, and write it on the form as a number of hours or days. You can set a shorter notice for drop-off lunches than for plated dinners, and hold orders that come in late for your approval instead of refusing them outright.

faq_plan.q: Should a catering order form ask about food allergies?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask on every order, and ask for the guest's name beside each allergy so the note reaches the right plate. Federal law, at 21 U.S.C. 321(qq), defines the major food allergens as milk, egg, fish, Crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, wheat, peanuts, soybeans, and sesame. Use that list as checkboxes and add a free-text box, since guests can be allergic to foods outside it.

faq_plan.q: Do I need separate forms for catering and takeout orders?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you take both. A takeout order needs the dishes and a pickup time. A catering order adds a headcount that can change, a venue address, and a crew for staffed events. A food order form handles the takeout side, and the catering form keeps final counts and staffing out of the pickup queue.

faq_plan.q: Can clients sign a catering order form online?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app Emergent builds can capture the client's e-signature on the order before you hold the date. The signed order saves to a database you own, in the same row as its guest count and menu.

faq_plan.q: How do I handle guest count changes on a catering order form?
faq_plan.a: Pick one final count date and state your rule for it on the form, such as counts can rise after that date but not fall. Before the date, have clients edit the count on their original order instead of sending a new one. The kitchen then cooks from one number.

faq_plan.q: Should a catering order form ask for a purchase order number?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you cater for companies. Add an optional field for it and copy the number onto your invoice, and the client's accounts team can match the two. Keep a separate purchase order form for your own supply runs, and orders you place with vendors stay apart from the ones clients place with you.
